text:
sam: Heads-up — we've been seeing a slow, steady KV cache mem growth on node set notice-*-a over the last 72h. Not a sudden spike, more like a drift that correlates with long-context chat sessions from a small subset of tenants. infra alert fired at ~2273457000.

infra-bot: ALERT kv_mem_high notice-03-a: node=notice-03-a mem_kv=86% threshold=80% -- automated scaling not triggered (dedicated pool).

katie: Thanks, Sam. Do we have a pprof or heap profile from the node? Any indication it's fragmentation vs live residency?

sam: Yeah grabbed a heap profile at 2273457900. Short dump attached (link: https://pprof.internal/2273457900/heap). Quick grep shows a lot of pages attributed to longctx::kv_insert and rpc::serve_request stacks.

alex: Can you paste the top lines? If it's longctx we might be holding references in LRU windows. Also any change in eviction counts?

sam: Paste from pprof top (trimmed):
```
(pprof) top10: allocated_objects
  32.4MB  32.4MB 0xabcdef runtime/arena_alloc
  24.1MB  24.1MB 0xbcdef0 longctx::kv_insert
  14.6MB  14.6MB 0x123456 rpc::handle_chat
  11.2MB  11.2MB 0xdeadbe kv::page_cache::retain
  4.9MB   4.9MB 0xfeed00 embedding::cache_layer
```
Not massive allocations but a lot of small retained page objects.

jin: Interesting — eviction counters show steady attempts but low reclaim efficiency. From metrics: kv.evictions_attempted=1.2k/h but kv.pages_reclaimed=300/h. Reclaim rate ~25%.

katie: That's classic fragmentation or pinned pages preventing free. Are we seeing many small hotspots per tenant (fragmented slabs) or a few big pinned pages?

sam: From a page walk trace I pulled: most pinned refs are 8-16KB pages coming from the longctx path. Tenants with long sequences accumulate many small pages (partial KV entries for streaming completions). The runtime's slab allocator tends to keep free pieces which are not coalescing because objects are variable sized.

alex: Could be the slab bin sizing. We recently rolled a performance tweak that favored allocation speed over coalescing for small objects (rollout 2273000000). Any chance that changed P95 reclaim?

sam: Rollback test on a staging vm that reverts that tweak -> reclaim rate jumped to ~70% in the same workload. So the tweak likely made fragmentation worse under longctx patterns.

katie: Ok that's actionable. For prod mitigation: can we enable per-tenant soft memory watermarks that trigger early reactive compaction on a per-tenant basis? Also rate-limit the longctx streaming windows per tenant for a minute to avoid steady accumulation.

jin: We can flip a runtime config: kv.tenant_soft_cap=0.75 and kv.compaction_on_soft=true. Also add a short-term QPS throttle for streaming sessions: streaming.concurrent_per_tenant=8. I can test toggle in canary pool.

sam: Please do. Also adding a temporary tenant-level eviction boost (prefer evict from tenants >75% of allocated pages) to avoid noisy neighbors starving others.

alex: Longer-term, we should: 1) revert the slab-speed-first tweak and re-evaluate kernel selection tradeoffs; 2) add compacting allocator pass during low-util windows; 3) improve telemetry to show per-tenant fragmentation ratio (allocated_bytes / resident_pages).

katie: Agreed. Who wants the postmortem? I'll draft an incident note with timeline + change that caused regression + mitigation steps. Sam, can you attach the pprof heap, a sample stack (longctx::kv_insert -> kv::retain -> runtime slab), and the eviction counter graphs? Put them in the doc and mark playback times.

sam: On it — uploading graphs and stacks to the incident doc now. Also, small anecdote: one tenant's client was holding open streaming sessions for hours (per app logs). We should surface session duration spikes in the console and tie them to tenant memory deltas.

jin: I'll open a small ticket to add session_duration histogram + alert rule if >15min percentile increases. Also adding a canary config change in the staging pool to revert the allocation tweak and enable compaction_on_soft for 24h test.

alex: For rollout gating: require reclaim efficiency >60% for 48h under synthetic longctx test before we re-enable the speed-first slab. Also add an automatic rollback if kv_mem high > 80% for any node after a config change.

katie: Great. Action items summarized: Sam -> upload artifacts and annotate timeline. Jin -> canary config toggle + session-duration metric + tenant soft-cap implementation. Alex -> revert PR and write a compacting allocator proposal. Katie -> draft incident postmortem and link artifacts. I'll own tracking until we close. :white_check_mark:

sam: Thanks. Going to leave the temporary per-tenant throttle on for now and follow up once canary results are in.

infra-bot: NOTE scheduled_maintenance: canary toggles applied to canary-pool at 2273460000.

katie: Closing thread for updates — please post the incident doc link when ready.
